requirements.evidence: All contract items are present: Queues.php:69-206 exposes the required properties/methods and view data (accessQueue, accessGrants at :216-219); Serve.php:40-43,62-99 has selectedQueueId/mode/lastCalledTicketId/notice and callNext; Members.php:38,77 adds activeTab/setActiveTab; routes/web.php:59-60 registers entity.queues/entity.serve; default-page.blade.php:44-53 adds both nav links; both lang files contain every required key. Slug re-derivation (Queues.php:142), the confirmation modal (queues.blade.php:103-124), scoped access data (Queues.php:216-219,238), waiting-list order/limit (Serve.php:168-173) and exception/rate-limit mapping (Serve.php:84-99) implement the stated edge cases.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess/CallNextTicket (Queues.php:83,133,166,223; Serve.php:84); #[Validate] on name/renameName/mode; #[Locked] on entity/lastCalledTicketId; policies are used for mount and actions; no migrations; CHANGELOG and docs/business-rules are updated. Deviation: grantAccess/revokeAccess (Queues.php:195-206) rely on SetQueueAccess instead of calling $this->authorize themselves, and most new public methods lack the PHPDoc the conventions ask for.

security.evidence: Entity-scoped findOrFail wherever writes happen (Queues.php:100,116,133,152,166,177,223-225; Serve.php:72); accessQueue()/viewingQueue() scope reads to the entity (:231-243); #[Locked] on entity and lastCalledTicketId (Serve.php:40-41); mode/name validated; all output uses {{ }}; rate limiting per user+entity (Serve.php:76-96); tests cover unauthorized calls, foreign ids, tampered state and the locked property. No exploitable weakness found; the access-modal render uses client-writable flags but the page mount is policy-gated (listed as a nit).

tests.evidence: New QueuesTest and ServeTest cover list/create/rename/toggle/access, waiting order/mode/30, call outcomes, rate limiting, unauthorized and tamper paths (QueuesTest.php:121-140,254-290; ServeTest.php:255-268,270-290,307,334-357); MembersTabsTest covers the tab behaviour; UiTranslationKeysTest checks key parity; existing tests were updated rather than weakened (EntityInviteTest.php:178-190; MembersTest.php:374-428). Gap: the waiting-list branch for a foreign/missing selectedQueueId is not tested, and closeAccess()/closeCreate() are not directly exercised.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses existing actions, x-label/x-input components and Bulma markup; private helpers keep the components small (Queues.php:223-252; Serve.php:115-173). Minor waste: Queues::render always loads all memberships (Queues.php:219) even when the access modal is closed.

readability.evidence: Clear names, focused methods and useful comments; the queues page follows the members page structure. Rough edges: access-modal role/grant logic sits in Blade with a fully-qualified App\Models\UserRole reference (queues.blade.php:138-140), and the serve notice is never cleared when the queue/mode changes (Serve.php:99; serve.blade.php:12,22).

scope.evidence: Only the three pages, their routes/navbar links, pt_BR/en strings, the business-rules/CHANGELOG docs and their tests are touched; no unrelated refactor or dependency changes.

issues.explanation: grantAccess() and revokeAccess() do not call $this->authorize('manageAccess', $queue) themselves; they rely on SetQueueAccess via setAccess() (Queues.php:223). Every other public action authorizes in the component, and the Livewire policy asks for that; impact is limited because SetQueueAccess authorizes server-side.

render() builds memberships and accessGrants from the client-writable managingAccess/accessQueueId, and accessQueue() only scopes the queue to the entity (Queues.php:238), without re-checking manageAccess. Mount gating limits exposure, but a retained component snapshot after a role change can still render the membership/grant list; gate the access view data on manageAccess.

The foreign-queue test only covers callNext; the requirement that a foreign/missing selectedQueueId shows no tickets and only ui.serve_empty in the waiting list is not asserted. closeAccess() and closeCreate() are also not exercised directly. Add these cases to the otherwise strong suite.
The memberships relation is loaded on every render even when the access modal is closed; load it only when managingAccess is true to avoid an unnecessary query on the list view.

The manager-role and grant lookup logic is embedded in Blade via @php, including a fully-qualified App\Models\UserRole reference; move it to a computed property or model helper so the view stays declarative and the namespace/logic is testable.

notice is only written by callNext(), so changing selectedQueueId or mode leaves a stale 'Now serving X.' message above the new queue/list; clear or qualify the notice when the selection or mode changes.

The detail modal's rename/deactivate/access buttons and the rename form's cancel/save buttons have no aria-label; they have visible text so their accessible names are fine, but the task's explicit aria-label requirement is only partly applied. Add labels or document that visible text is the accessible name.

review.summary: Adds the tenant queues management page and attendant serve panel, splits the members page into tabs, and wires routes, navbar links, pt_BR/en strings, docs and a broad Pest suite. The implementation matches the task and contract and is secure by construction (entity-scoped lookups, locked server state, rate limiting, unauthorized/tamper tests), with only minor nits: grant/revoke delegate authorization to the action, the access-modal view data trusts client flags, a few UI/test edge cases are uncovered, and the view holds some role logic. Approve with nits.
